title: Four Disrupted Continuations
takeaway: In ordinary pretraining-like text, J-space ablation selectively destroys the predictions that depend on a silently assembled characterization of the context — an acronym's memorized expansion, a 1914 wage figure, a botanist's identity, an imaging method's clinical framing — while copying, syntax, and generic continuation survive. In each panel the ablated lens directions name exactly the contextual characterization the broken prediction needed.
walkthrough:
The item is a live, hoverable widget, not a static image. It holds four panels, each a passage of pretraining-like text run under [[j-space-ablation]]: at every token position, across a band of layers, the [[residual-stream]]'s projections onto the ten most active [[j-lens-vector]] directions are zeroed — sparing any token already in the clean top-10 predictions, so the intervention targets internal content rather than the output itself. Two panels use the light setting and two the medium setting of the three [[ablation-strengths]].

Each passage's tokens are shaded by the [[kl-divergence]] between the clean and ablated next-token distributions at that position, from white (no change) to orange (the panel's maximum). Hovering a token fills three columns: Top Ablated, the ten lens directions removed there; Before, the clean model's prediction probabilities; After, the ablated model's, with the KL in the header. Each panel opens on its most disrupted position, and an Analysis note in the corner gives the authors' reading.

The four opening positions break the same way. In "CONSORT acronym", the model expands "Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials" with *reporting* at probability 1.00; the ablated directions are the paper's topic (*radio*, *lung*, *heating*, *thermal*, *electrode*), and without them the model outputs *random* at 0.99 — what such trials are about, not what the acronym spells. In "1914 MA minimum wage", the ablated directions are the full retrieval key — *massachusetts*, *boston*, *wages*, *minimum*, *weekly*, *women* — and the memorized cents of $8.71 fall from 0.64 to a spread of round-cent guesses led by *50* at 0.12. In "Species epithet", removing South American geography plus *botan* and *ernst* turns the genitive *ei* of the Brazilian botanist Hoehne (1.00) into the higher-frequency ending *ii* (0.96) — valid Latin for the wrong person. In "Shear-wave techniques", removing the diagnostic framing (*diagnosis*, *detection*, *breast*) flips *Elastography* (1.00), the clinical modality, to *Dispersion* (0.89), its physics sibling.

The survivals are visible in the shading. Most positions stay near white, consistent with the section's report that the [[pretraining-top-1-match]] stays high overall. The second "$8.71" a few tokens after the first is unaffected: it is copied by induction from the first occurrence and needs no contextual retrieval. The panels put the paper's [[flexible-vs-automatic-dissociation]] on raw text: contextually inferred predictions collapse to a generic prior, and automatic ones proceed untouched.

terms.definition: The first panel (light ablation): a clinical-trial write-up citing the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials, where the model must produce "Reporting", the R of the acronym, and after ablation produces "random" instead.

The second panel (light ablation): a 1914 economics address in which a Massachusetts wage board totals a working woman's weekly budget to $8.71; the model must produce the cents "71" at the decimal point.
The third panel (medium ablation): a list of Arachis (peanut) species in which the model must complete "hoehnei", the Latin genitive of the surname of the Brazilian botanist Frederico Carlos Hoehne.

The fourth panel (medium ablation): a diagnostic-ultrasound paper title in which the model must choose "Elastography", the clinical shear-wave modality, and after ablation chooses "Dispersion", the physics-oriented variant.

The panel tags naming which of the paper's three J-space ablation strengths was applied; the strengths differ in the range of layers over which the top-10 lens directions are projected out, and are defined in Figure 22.

The left column under each passage: the ten J-lens directions zeroed at the hovered position, ranked 1 to 10 by activation strength. These are the tokens whose lens components the intervention removed there.
The middle column: the unablated model's next-token probability distribution at the hovered position, drawn as labeled bars.
The right column: the ablated model's next-token distribution at the same position; the header carries the KL divergence between the two distributions.
The KL divergence between the clean and ablated next-token distributions at a position — the widget's measure of how much the ablation disturbed the prediction there.

Each passage token's background color encodes the KL caused by ablating at that position, on a white-to-orange ramp normalized to the panel's maximum; near-white tokens are positions the ablation barely touched.
A hover tooltip in each panel's top-right corner containing the authors' interpretation of that example.

One vector per vocabulary token per layer: the direction encoding the model's disposition to say that token. The ablation removes the residual stream's components along the ten most active of these at each position.

Marker glyphs in the token strip standing for tokenizer bookkeeping — capitalization, space, uppercase, and newline markers — kept visible so that marker-only tokens can still be hovered. The CONSORT and shear-wave panels' key tokens are such markers, sitting immediately before the word being predicted.
A leading ellipsis showing that the displayed passage starts partway into its source document.

numbers.meaning: Panels in the figure, one per example; the section names their common shape: a clinical paper's topic, a quoted speech's historical setting, a botanist's nationality, and an imaging technique's diagnostic-versus-physics framing.
J-lens directions ablated at each token position — the k = 10 most strongly activated lens vectors, excluding any token already in the clean forward pass's top-10 predictions.
KL divergence at the CONSORT panel's key position (just before "Reporting"), the panel's maximum — the most disrupted position in that passage.

In the CONSORT panel, the clean model puts probability 1.00 on "reporting"; the ablated model puts 0.99 on "random" — it reconstructs the acronym's R from what trials are about rather than recalling what it spells.
KL at the decimal point of "$8.71" in the wage panel — the passage's most disrupted position, though smaller than the other panels' maxima because the clean prediction was already uncertain.
The clean model's probability on "71", the correct cents of the memorized wage figure — the model is only moderately confident even unablated, per the Analysis note.
The ablated model's probabilities on "50", "00", "75", "25": with the retrieval key removed, it reverts to a round-cent prior spread over plausible amounts.
The weekly minimum living wage proposed at the 1914 Massachusetts wage-board hearing; its second occurrence in the passage is unaffected by ablation because induction copies it from the first.
The year of the economics address the wage passage quotes — part of the historical setting the workspace must assemble.
KL at the token "hn" inside "hoehnei" in the species panel, that panel's maximum.

In the species panel, the clean model puts 1.00 on the ending "ei" (the genitive for Hoehne); ablated, 0.96 goes to "ii", the statistically commoner species-epithet ending — a one-letter error naming the wrong person.
KL at the position before "Elastography" in the shear-wave panel, that panel's maximum.
In the shear-wave panel, the clean model puts 1.00 on "elast(ography)"; ablated, 0.89 goes to "disp(ersion)" — a real sibling technique, chosen once the diagnostic-use cue is gone.
